messages.subject: [statnet_help] Combining UCINET Adj.Matrices with categorical data in excel
messages.subject_clean: [statnet_help] Combining UCINET Adj.Matrices with categorical data in excel
messages.body_plain:
Dear Statneters,

I am a relative newcomer to R and am looking to merge my work in networks
with the conventional scale data I have on an organisation (p=58).
I have a large number of processed binary adjacency matrices developed in
UCINET, which I can output as excel files. I also have a large number of
data frames within excel files.
The AM's and the excel files all share a common coding so 1 identifies the
same person in the network as it does in the attribute dataframes.

I would like to explore how much of the network analysis I can do in
Statnet/R. At present I am finding it hard to know how I might most
conveniently link the AM's to the various categorical data I have (e.g.
personality, values, perceived trustworthiness and so on).
I would like to be able to carry out both ego and network correlations and
regressions.
For example I might want to regress personality profile on network
centrality (there is not uniformity of number of edges between the network
data and the attribute data, some attribute data may apply to a subset of
the network e.g. managers).

I have looked through a number of the supporting documents, and found
'Network Analysis with statnet for Individual , Organizational , and
International Relations Applications' to be particularly helpful.
But, it looks as though I would need to code each attribute link
individually which would not be practical.
My guess (fervent hope...) is that there is a simple way of knitting these
data together that I have not registered.

Please don't hesitate to ask if more information/clarification is needed.

Any help or link to a suitable document on this would make my jubilee
weekend!

Best,
Nick Duncan
University of Cambridge

messages.subject_clean: [statnet_help] RE: Combining UCINET Adj.Matrices with categorical data in excel
messages.body_plain:
Hi Nick
I may be misinterpreting what you mean by "link," but I can suggest how you can create a network object with an arbitrarily large number of vertex attributes.
I find it convenient to save my Excel network-related data as CSV files and import into R.  For the adjacency matrix, be sure that the first COLUMN is NOT the names/numbers of the nodes, but the first ROW can be (and perhaps should be, if you want to keep the vertex names you provide). You need not specify each node attribute singly, but can read it in as a table, and use the "vertex.attr" option when creating your network object in R.

nodeData <- read.csv("C:\\Path\\nodeData.csv",header=T)  # read in node data
adjMat <- read.csv("C:\\Path\\AdjacencyMatrix.csv",header=T)  # read in adjacency matrix
nodeData$nodeNames <- names(adjMat)  # add a "nodeNames" variable to the node data populated with the vertex names from the first row of the adjacency matrix file
myNetwork <- network(as.matrix(adjMat),vertex.attr=nodeData, directed=?)  # create a network object with the node data - specify directed=T or F as appropriate
myNetwork # see a description of the network object including a listing of the node data variables

Cheers,
Brian Rubineau

messages.subject: [statnet_help] Vertex.Col: A problem and a question
messages.subject_clean: [statnet_help] Vertex.Col: A problem and a question
messages.body_plain:
Dear All,


Thanks to your help, I am now hapily creating network objects with
attribute data that look plausible.
My first steps have been to visualise some attribute data within different
networks.
Having overcome (I hope) the issue of having missing data in the
attributes, by suppressing the relevant rows in the attribute matrix, I'd
like to be quite sure about the interpretation that can be made of the
colour of the node markers.

I have used plot.network which seems very flexible.
'vertex.col="HH" where HH is a range of scores between 1 and 5.

I am having one problem and have one question.

Problem: I cannot understand the logic of the colour selection, and what
colour is assigned to the nodes with missing attibute data. In a test it
seemed that white/no colour was assigned to zero or missing data). However
in the real data, a grey scale seems to have been adopted with white/no
colour being a high score.

I can't see a way of configuring vertex.col - should I perhaps use a
different plot command such as gplot? It would be important to be able to
assign a specific colour to the missing data to avoid confusion.

My question: Could I get a heatmap type colouring in the node marker (which
has the nice option of using either relative or absolute scores)?

Many thanks for any pointer on this.

Nick Duncan
Centre of Development Studies
University of Cambridge

messages.subject: [statnet_help] texreg: ergm output --> LaTeX (for multiple models)
messages.subject_clean: [statnet_help] texreg: ergm output --> LaTeX (for multiple models)
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I thought I should share my latest R package with you since it works 
quite well with the ergm package.

I frequently have to copy and paste coefficients, standard errors, 
significance levels and AIC, BIC etc. manually into my LaTeX papers. I 
usually have several models which should be merged into a single table, 
and I didn't really find a good solution for this problem. There is of 
course the apsrtable package, but it does not accept ergm objects 
(except for a quick and dirty hack I found somewhere on the web).

In case you encounter the same difficulties and want a simple solution, 
you may want to take a look at my new R package texreg, which converts 
the output of ergm, lm, lme, glm and gls objects into fancy LaTeX 
tables. The project website is located here:

http://r-forge.r-project.org/projects/texreg/

The current version is already on CRAN, but it may take a few days until 
it is available on all mirrors and until you can install it regularly by 
entering install.packages("texreg"). In the meantime, you can use the 
r-forge repository and enter install.packages("texreg", 
repos="http://R-Forge.R-project.org").

The package is easily customizable for other model types (maybe someone 
would like to work with me on latentnet ergmm objects or other model 
types?). It also works well in conjunction with Sweave. The 
documentation is available here:

http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/texreg/vignettes/texreg.pdf

Best regards

Philip
